svg.title: Figure 2 · Who runs which part, by how you reach the model
svg.desc: Five panels, each repeating Figure 1: chat app, coding assistant, API, open weights, and a lab-internal research run (the incident). Fill shows who runs each part: vendor-run (blue), yours (teal), or shared; an asterisk marks a part the lab had and did not run. Left of each panel's harness, a user-interface column lists chat tool, code tool, API and other, joined to the harness by a two-way arrow; the cell for that panel's way in carries its owner's fill (chat app: chat tool, vendor; coding assistant: code tool, vendor; API: API, yours; open weights: other, yours; lab-internal run: other, the lab) and the other three are grey.
svg.text: Figure 2 · Who runs which part, by how you reach the model
vendor-built; you or your org set it
you build the harness, or the vendor hosts it
the releaser; any fine-tune is yours
vendor-run (the lab, in the last panel)
yours: you or your org builds or sets it
shared: two fills, both parts named
Each panel repeats Figure 1: the model unit on top
(training, model, model safeguards); the run below
placement per mode is this series' reading,
* The lab had this monitor and did not run it.
Several parts were off or reduced for the
evaluation; the incident paper covers them.
